searches.answer: The sources indicate that in 2026, machine learning trends will focus on automation, speed, efficiency, and specialization, with a shift towards making machine learning more affordable and versatile for businesses of all sizes. Key trends include federating learning, which is vital for sectors like healthcare and finance due to compliance requirements; multimodal machine learning (MML) that aims to understand the "why" behind tasks; and the rise of generative models for complex content generation, which raises ethical concerns. Other trends mentioned are autonomous decision-making, machine learning operationalization management (MLOps), AI and sustainability, quantum ML, explainable AI (XAI), edge AI, AI-generated content, and the use of AI in healthcare. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to all specific trends or technologies.

searches.query: new data science tools and frameworks
searches.answer: The sources mention several new data science tools and frameworks for 2026. Streamlit is highlighted as an open-source framework for creating custom data science applications and dashboards, simplifying the process of building interactive apps using Python scripts. Apache Arrow is noted for revolutionizing data storage and transfer for big data applications, accelerating data processing with its in-memory columnar format. Apache Spark is recognized as a powerhouse for big data processing, supporting batch processing and streaming data analysis across multiple programming languages. Other frameworks mentioned include RandomForest, Xgboost, LightGBM, Fast.ai, ONNX, Jupyter Notebook, Amazon SageMaker for Data Scientists, Google Cloud Datalab, Pandas, and Spark MLib. These tools and frameworks are part of the evolving landscape of data science, offering various functionalities from machine learning tool prototyping to big data processing and analysis.
